(1) the Mn atoms are predominantly substitutional in GaMnNAs and GaMnSb, and that (2) the interstitial Mn atoms are predominantly surrounded by As in GaMnS and GaMnAs.
the Mn interstitials are the most common defects in as-grown GaMnAs and that the interstitials have As nearest neighbors.
(i) interstitial Mn atoms are found to be the dominant Mn defect in GaMnAssynthesized by molecular beam epitaxy and (ii) the interstitial Mn atoms have As nearest neighbors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic, magnetic and structural properties of GaMnAs and other dilute magnetic semiconductors.
the development and application of new experimental methods for the investigation of the structure of semiconductor alloys.
the determination of the concentration of minority constituents in GaMn As by combining structure factor measurements and X-ray analysis in the TEM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the as-grown GaMnAs layers contain a large amount of Mn interstitial defects, which are predominantly bound to As atoms.
interstitial Mn is present in GaMnAS in a concentration comparable to antisite defects, which are in a comparable amount to that of substitutional Mn.
the interstitials are present in the as-grown layers in concentrations of the order of 0.1%, with As nearest neighbors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interstitials and substitutional Mn are the dominant Mn atoms in GaMnAssub>0.05 and that the interstitial Mn atoms are the dominant minority constituent in GaMnAsub>0.05.
the local concentrations of As antisite defects and substitutional Mn are small in as-grown GaMnAs and the interstitials have As nearest neighbors.
the local Mn concentrations are not homogeneous in the as-grown layers, but that the interstitials and substitutional Mn are spatially correlated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interstitials are present in as-grown GaMnAs, and that their concentrations and locations are determined by the growth conditions.
interstitial Mn is an important defect species in GaMn As.
